keySource: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards on page 38 of the released-items PDF -- which is a materially different situation from RegentsAlign, where the key lives in a separate scoring-key document and had to be derived independently first. Here the item map IS the official publication, and it is the same table this project's item data comes from. Three things guard it. First, tools/preflight.py re-derives every multiple-choice key by a second, unrelated code path -- a naive plain-reading-order re-read of the PDF with no geometry at all -- and compares; across the twelve tests that is 282 keys with no disagreement. Second, the NYCPS 'NYS Exam IM Alignment' sheets in sources/nycps/ independently agree with our standard for 256 of 273 items on the 2023-2025 tests, and where they differ ours is the more precise reading. Third, several items were checked arithmetically against the decoded content rather than taken on trust: item 15's choices decode to -8/15, -3/40, 3/40, 8/15 and -1/5 x 3/8 = -3/40, which is choice B and matches the published key; item 21's choices differ only by their inequality symbol and decode to 20x+5<=200, 20x+5<200, 5x+20>=200, 5x+20>200, of which 5x+20>=200 is the artist earning at least $200, which is choice C and matches. NOT claimed: that all 34 answers were solved from scratch before the key was consulted.

reviewNotes: Item 27's variable y in 'the amount of juice, y, that can be made' is missing from the stem: the glyph sits inside the graph's own bounding box, so the figure-zone exclusion takes it. Left as a known gap rather than hand-patched, because hand-patching the stem would break the prose-fidelity check that makes this data trustworthy.
Item 7's repeating-decimal overbar covers '.3' rather than just the '3', so 3.3-repeating renders with the bar one character too wide.

Item 47 is a displayed expression published as an image rather than as text. It reads correctly; it is simply less good than markup would be. Item 20 was in the same state until wide fraction bars were admitted to the glyph table, and now renders as text.
Item 31's displayed expression decodes as '(5.2 - 1.6) + (---) = 0', where the three rules are an answer box rather than minus signs.
Items 43's two stray '.50' and '.25' fragments are pieces of its pizza-price list that escaped the figure zone.

Two of the 42 stems carry a trailing artifact from their answer line, which in these two items shares a prose line with the end of the question: item 40 ends '...should Mr. Morgano receive? $' and item 45 ends '...in the sixth grade? Answerstudents'. Left visible rather than hand-patched, because editing a stem would break the prose-fidelity check that makes this data trustworthy -- the fix belongs in the extractor's line classification.
